h: Sacred Eating Engraves the Torah Upon the Heart

p: "This is the statute of the Torah."
that the words of Torah be engraved in the heart.
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
to rectify the corruption of the Nachash,
which brought death to the world.
And the beginning of the corruption of the Nachash
was in the matter of eating,
and the sensing of one's own pleasure;
and afterward it came upon Chavah
and this is the kelipah of desire.
And afterward from this branched out
of the corruption of the Nachash
is the One who feeds and sustains,
and then the holiness is engraved in the heart
to rectify the corruption of the Nachash.
And this is what it says in the Mechilta
And this is what the holy Zohar says
"the law of the kingdom is law,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קיח, א)
the words of Torah will be engraved in the heart,
to rectify the corruption of the Nachash.
rather through the delight of Shabbos
for all that a person eats
And as is written in the holy Zohar
"'May He send your help from the sanctuary' (Tehillim 20:3)
this is the washing of the hands, etc.;
'and may He accept your burnt-offering, selah' (Tehillim 20:4)
this is the blessing of zimun."
And this is as they said
these are the last waters, etc.;
is the One who gives bread
And this is what it says:
"May He send your help from the sanctuary"
that is, help against the yetzer hara,
"And were it not that Hakadosh Baruch Hu
יִתֶּן לְךָ כִלְבָבֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר (תְּהִלִּים כ, ה)
'May He give you according to your heart, etc.'" (Tehillim 20:5);
whose heart is whole before his Creator,
the will of the Creator, blessed be His Name,
And afterward it is stated in the holy Zohar:
this is the Kiddusha Rabba, etc.";
it helps to rectify the corruption,
And so it is stated in the Gemara
is given the requests of his heart."
And this is as it says:
"May He give you according to your heart,
(and this has been explained many times).

paragraphs.text: Source: Sukkah 52b — “רע כל היום״. אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: יצרו של אדם מתגבר עליו בכל יום ומבקש להמיתו, שנאמר: ״צופה רשע לצדיק ומבקש להמיתו״, ואלמלא הקדוש ברוך הוא שעוזר לו — …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 116) — “evil all day” (Genesis 6:5). All day long his thoughts and desires are for evil. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s evil inclination overcomes him each day and seeks to kill him, as it stated: “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him” (Psalms 37:32); the wicked here is referring to the wickedness inside one’s heart. And if not for the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who assists him with the good …”
